problems.form_value: name_model 'GPT-4o (same setup as the main study)'; how_used 'Same four approaches as S1'; each arm described 'as in S1'
problems.source_says: Appendix D names no model, interface, or approach for the pilot. 'The same procedure and platforms' opens the recruitment sentence. Four approaches follow only from arithmetic (12 per problem, 3 per cell). That the pilot used GPT-4o and the S1 interfaces is an inference, not a statement. S1's eligibility does not depend on it.
problems.quote: Using the same procedure and platforms as for the main study, we recruited 36 people ... and randomly assigned three participants to each design problem and approach (i.e., each problem was reframed by 12 participants).

problems.form_value: open_chat (study level, justified by codebook section 8, rule 3)
problems.source_says: Open chat describes only FREE-FORM (58 of the 218 analyzed LLM-arm participants). DIRECT (72) and STRUCTURED (88) used button interfaces with fixed prompts that hand participants GPT-4o frames, which the form's own arm entries code ideas_supplied. Codebook section 8, rule 3 picks the arm for the primary record. It does not set a study-level role, so the DIRECT and STRUCTURED contrasts carry a role that does not describe them. Coding convention only. Eligibility is unaffected.
problems.quote: While users converse freely with the agent in the free-form setting, the direct and structured ones should guide users to employ particular methods with the models.
problems.locator: p. 17, Appendix A, second paragraph; arm counts p. 9, Figure 8 (table at right)

confirmed.statement: The paper says assignment was random in five places: 'randomly assigned participants to one of the approaches and problems' (p. 2), 'We randomly assigned participants to one of the conditions' (Section 4), 'balanced Latin square randomization' (Section 4.1), the 'Randomized' node and 'Each was randomly assigned an approach' (Figure 4), and 'randomly assigned a reframing approach and problem' (Section 4.5).
confirmed.locator: p. 2, left column, third paragraph; p. 5, Section 4 and Section 4.1; p. 6, Figure 4 and caption; p. 7, Section 4.5, first paragraph

confirmed.statement: The form's S1 assignment quote is verbatim, and its four locators (p. 5, Sections 4.1 and 4; p. 6, Figure 4 caption; p. 7, Section 4.5) are right.

The only description of the mechanism is 'balanced Latin square randomization', a counterbalancing term the paper does not explain for a between-subjects design. Every other mention says 'randomly assigned', so randomized = yes rests on the paper's own words.

Each participant received one approach and one problem in a between-subjects design with four levels. So unit = individual and structure = between are right, and no order of conditions needs checking.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 4.1; p. 7, Section 4.5, first paragraph

confirmed.statement: What was assigned is a way of doing the participant's own reframing task (no LLM, or one of three ways of using GPT-4o) plus one of three problems. Participants could submit LLM frames as given or build on them, and raters scored the frame each participant picked as best. Conditions do not differ only in whose output gets evaluated.
confirmed.locator: p. 6, Section 4.3, 'Task instructions'; p. 7, Section 4.5; p. 8, Section 5, first paragraph

confirmed.statement: The tool is generative AI. All three LLM arms used OpenAI's GPT-4o ('the tests used only GPT-4o'). FREE-FORM used the default ChatGPT on the participant's own account ('the model was the same for all users: GPT-4o'), and submitted conversation logs confirmed its use.
confirmed.locator: p. 2, left column, second paragraph; p. 7, Section 4.5, second paragraph; p. 13, Section 6.4; p. 17, Appendix A

confirmed.statement: Comparison arm: MANUAL is 'a baseline condition wherein designers reframe problems without using LLMs'. So arms[MANUAL].ai = none and the ai_vs_bau label fit, and the ai_design contrasts compare GPT-4o configurations. The paper describes no instruction or check that kept MANUAL participants from using AI on their own.

The S1 arm descriptions match the source. DIRECT: a 'Reframe' button and two fixed prompts. STRUCTURED: a nine-step prompt chain with regeneration within each step and an option to add one's own content. FREE-FORM: own-account ChatGPT with a submitted conversation log.
confirmed.locator: p. 17, Appendix A.1; p. 18, Figure 12 and Table 4; p. 19, Appendix A.2; p. 20, Figure 14 caption; p. 7, Section 4.5

confirmed.statement: Analyzed counts in the PDF table match arms[].n_analyzed: MANUAL 62, DIRECT 72, STRUCTURED 88, FREE-FORM 58, total 280. The three LLM arms sum to the 218 in the pooled LLM group.
confirmed.locator: p. 9, Figure 8 (table at right); p. 9, Section 5.2

confirmed.statement: All 456 recruits pass through the 'Randomized' node, and 456 frames were collected before filtering, so the 176 exclusions came after assignment. No per-arm randomized count is printed, so arms[].n_randomized = null is right.
confirmed.locator: p. 6, Figure 4 and caption; p. 6, Section 4.2, first paragraph

confirmed.statement: People assigned to an LLM arm who did not use the LLM were removed, and MANUAL has no matching rule. The form records this. It weakens the analyzed comparison but does not change the fact that assignment was random.
Expertise was balanced across arms in the analyzed sample: chi-squared(3, N = 280) = 0.70, p = 0.87.
No preregistration is mentioned anywhere in the document, so preregistered = not_stated is right.

S2 (pilot): the paper states random assignment of 36 people, three to each problem-and-approach cell and 12 per problem, in a between-subjects layout. S2 is below 50 people and reports no comparison by condition, so it cannot affect eligibility.

summary: The PDF supports the core assignment coding: individual designers were randomly assigned, between subjects, to reframe one of three problems without an LLM (MANUAL) or with GPT-4o in one of three ways, and the arms, tool, and analyzed counts match the source (pp. 2, 5-7, 9, 17-20), so criterion 1 holds. The coding is refuted on details only: Appendix D does not say the pilot (S2) used GPT-4o or the S1 interfaces, and the study-level role open_chat fits only the FREE-FORM arm and rests on a codebook rule that governs primary records, not this field.
